native_retrieval.title: Delhi HC asks NCERT to respond to plea challenging online bids from empanelled firms, ETLegalWorld
native_retrieval.snippet: The Delhi High Court has sought response of the Centre and the NCERT on a plea challenging online bids from firms currently empanelled for supply of items of the new kit 'Jaadui Pitara' developed by the organisation. The petition claimed that the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) while issuing corrigendum has set the one-sided and biased criteria of eligibility conditions and other requirements for bidders. The plea was listed before a vacation bench of Justice Amit Mahajan which asked the Ministry of Education and NCERT to file reply to the petition. Petitioner Samit Khanna, proprietor of Universal Sales, who has been dealing in manufacturing and distribution of toys since 2013 and registered under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, said he meets all the criteria set out by NCERT except the criteria of empanelled firm. native_retrieval.title: Non Participants in Tender Process Cannot Challenge Award Delhi HC | LawStreet
native_retrieval.snippet: Home Judiciary [Non Participants in Tender Process Cannot Challenge Award: Delhi HC [Read Judgement]](/judiciary/non-participants-in-tender-process-cannot-challenge-award-delhi-hc). # Non Participants in Tender Process Cannot Challenge Award: Delhi HC [Read Judgement]. Non Participants in Tender Process Cannot Challenge Award Delhi HC. **New Delhi:** The Delhi High Court has recently dismissed a petition challenging the award of a tender by Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) for an oil pipeline project. The court noted that the petitioner, Primatel Fibcom Ltd, had not participated in the bidding process and only intended to supply equipment to one of the bidders. *Only the entities who participate in the tender process pursuant to a tender notice can be allowed to make grievances about the non-fulfilment or breach of any of the terms and conditions of the tender documents concerned. The respondent who chose to stay away from the tender process cannot be heard to whittle down, in any manner, the rights of the eligible bidders who had participated in the tender process on the basis of the written and express terms and conditions.*.
